messages:
OpsBot: incident alert: host-rw-12 OOM during KV cache page-in (pid=4421). auto-restart triggered :rotating_light:
Maya R: seeing this in canary? which model/seq?
Chris T: yes, canary q2 on dedicated pool. seq_len peaked around 28k, batch size 4. KV hit ratio dropped then memory climbed ~+18% over 10m.
Lee (runtime): quick profiler dump attached (trimmed):
```
kv_pages_allocated: 18.9GB -> 22.3GB
kv_frag_bytes: 2.1GB
page_faults/sec: 420
compaction_cycles: 0
kernel_selected: int8-avx2 (fallback path for long-seq)
batch_delay_ms: 12 -> 45
```
Sam P: weird that compaction_cycles=0. we recently disabled background compaction for canary to avoid CPU spikes.
Anya S: that aligns — no compaction + long ctx + batching growth -> fragmentation and uncollected slabs. OOM footprint is fragment + reservation headroom.
David L: also noticing kernel switch to int8-avx2 path. can that increase KV page residency because of different kv packing?
Lee (runtime): yes, kernel selection changed per sequence length policy. AVX path uses wider per-token cache layout with slightly larger per-key metadata. On long sequences that multiplies.
Maya R: what are short-term mitigations? we need canary to stay up and not roll back if possible.
Chris T: immediate ideas: 1) re-enable periodic compaction on canary with CPU cap, 2) reduce max batch delay for that pool, 3) force kernel policy to compact-friendly variant for >16k contexts, 4) soft-evict older prefixes earlier.
Lee (runtime): I pushed a patch to enable lightweight compaction (throttle=0.3) on canary nodes. rolling to 3 hosts now.
Sam P: added a temporary quota flag: `kv.soft_limit=20GB` + eviction-on-alloc. will drop oldest non-pinned spans first.
Anya S: careful: eviction-on-alloc might regress latency for hot sessions. recommend staggered evict with prefetch hints.
David L: also enabling fallback: if allocation fails, try a degraded path that disables KV lookups for that request and marks session for rewarm. minimal perf hit but keeps requests alive.
Maya R: can we add a metric/alert to detect when kernel switch correlates with kv growth? want to catch before OOM.
Lee (runtime): yes — adding metric: kv_growth_rate_by_kernel and a rule: if growth_rate>50MB/min and kernel != baseline then page an oncall.
Chris T: tests: recreated locally by forcing kernel switch + disabling compaction. repro sequence attached: `repro/longctx-kernel-swap-2026.sh` (small script to simulate). repro triggers fragmentation in ~45s.
Maya R: plan for next 2 hours: 1) let lightweight compaction finish rolling, 2) apply kv.soft_limit on remaining canary hosts, 3) enable degraded-kv fallback, 4) monitor kv_growth_rate_by_kernel alert for 30m, 5) if still unstable -> temporary pin kernel to compact-friendly.
Anya S: logging change request: when eviction happens, log top-3 session prefixes and kernel id. helps root cause whether specific prompt patterns cause fragmentation.
David L: added: `--kv-evict-reason=soft_limit` + prefix hashes in logs. will be included in next deploy.
Sam P: monitoring shows hosts with compaction enabled dropped fragment bytes from ~2.1GB -> 0.4GB and growth stabilised. current memory trending down on those 3 hosts.
Maya R: great. leaving canary open for another hour. if stable we'll roll change to dedicated pool with gradual ramp. thanks all :+1:
OpsBot: deploy events: compaction-toggle v2 -> host-rw-10 host-rw-11 host-rw-12 [in-progress]
Chris T: follow-ups: we should add a unit test that simulates kernel selection variance + long context to catch per-key-layout regressions in future.
Lee (runtime): noted. i'll add an integration test that toggles kernel policy under load and checks KV fragmentation delta.
Maya R: capture runbook steps in the incident page and mark postmortem SLA. i'll own the doc.
David L: postmortem checklist: timeline, kernel map, compaction config, batch heuristics, affected sessions and mitigation impact.
Anya S: thanks everyone. small win: compaction + soft_limit + degraded fallback kept canary alive without full rollback.
Sam P: logging/alerts tickets: ENG-RUNTIME-873 (metric+alert), ENG-RUNTIME-874 (evict logs), ENG-RUNTIME-875 (integration test).
Maya R: closing thread for now. re-open if regressions.
